podcast.title: Early Career and Christian Roots (1992)
podcast.body: Formed in 1992, all members of P.O.D. are "born again" Christians. Their manager previously operated a Christian rock club in San Diego. The band's early career involved playing numerous youth group concerts in churches and community centers, eventually expanding across the country. "When they started up in 1992 POD began by playing all the youth group concerts at churches and community centers in their area and then across the country."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Ozzfest Tour (2000)
podcast.body: By the summer of 2000, P.O.D., a band composed of born-again Christians, embarked on a tour with Ozzy Osbourne, known as the "Prince of Darkness," as part of Ozzfest. This unusual pairing was humorously characterized as "sabotaging Satan's music from the inside." "By the summer of 2000s this band of born again was on the road with the Prince of Darkness, Ozzy Osborne and that year's version of Osfest."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Atlantic Records Signing
podcast.body: The band's substantial fanbase, cultivated through performances in Christian-friendly clubs across the U.S., ultimately led to their discovery and signing by Atlantic Records. P.O.D. became one of the pioneering bands to successfully cross over from the "Christian Underground" into the mainstream "Heathen Rock" world. "Eventually and thanks to the network of fans POD had amassed in the Christian friendly clubs across the US they were discovered and signed by Atlantic Records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Born Again Members
podcast.body: All members of P.O.D. are born again Christians, a fact that is not immediately apparent from their appearance, which includes tattoos and long hair. "All the members of the band are born again."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Criticism from within Christian community
podcast.body: P.O.D. has been subject to condemnation by some individuals who believe that Christian bands, regardless of their message, are perverting Christianity by playing rock music. "And they spend lots of time quoting scripture to support their opinions on the evils and perversions of Creed and jars of clay and MXPX and everybody else."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Career & Manager
podcast.body: The band's manager previously operated a Christian rock club in San Diego. P.O.D. formed in 1992 and initially built their career by performing at youth group concerts in churches and community centers across the country. They independently sold 40,000 copies of three self-released EPs. "When they started up in 1992, POD began by playing all the youth group concerts at churches and community centers in their area and then across the country."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mainstream Crossover Appeal
podcast.body: P.O.D. successfully attracted a substantial number of mainstream rock fans due to their positive yet non-preachy lyrics and genuinely powerful rock sound. By the late 1990s, they were receiving various local music awards. "Because they were simply positive and not preachy with their lyrics and because they really rocked POD managed to attract a substantial number of mainstream rock fans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mainstream Crossover Success
podcast.body: P.O.D. attracted a significant number of mainstream rock fans due to their positive but not preachy lyrics and their strong rock sound. By the late 1990s, they were winning local music awards. In summer 2000, they toured with Ozzy Osbourne on Ozzfest, leading to their signing with Atlantic Records. They are considered one of the first major crossovers from the Christian Underground to mainstream "Heathen Rock." "POD became one of the first major crossovers from the Christian Underground into the mainstream world of Heathen Rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-9/11 Popularity
podcast.body: The album "Satellite" was released on September 11th, 2001. It is suggested that the timing of its release, amidst the attacks on New York and Washington, may have contributed to its popularity as people sought positive messages. "Then again, maybe the attacks on New York and Washington helped POD become even more popular."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Self-Released EPs Success
podcast.body: Through their extensive performances at Christian-friendly venues, P.O.D. managed to sell an impressive 40,000 copies of three self-released NDEPs (likely EPs). "in the process they managed to sell 40,000 copies of the three self-released NDEPs which certainly wasn't bad."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unaware Mainstream Audience
podcast.body: Many mainstream listeners enjoyed P.O.D.'s music without knowing about the band's Christian roots, focusing instead on the quality of their rock sound. "In fact, it's possible that you just heard for the first time that POD was a Christian rock band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Undisclosed Christian Roots
podcast.body: A notable aspect of P.O.D.'s mainstream success was that many fans became engaged with their music without realizing the group's Christian background, simply enjoying them as a great rock band making great music. "But here's the thing, people got into POD without even knowing the group's Christian roots. All they cared about was that this was a great rock band that made great music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
